provenance: Hand-written SYNTHETIC fixtures by Person 3 (Vatsal). Company names and values are invented. Expected outcomes were derived by hand (see each 'derivation') before running D1. These demonstrate implementation behaviour only; they are not benchmark data and do not estimate detection rates.

cases.description: Clean table whose total adds up; prose agrees with the table.

detector_input.pre_text: ACME Corp revenue by type is shown below.
detector_input.post_text: Total revenue was $1.5 billion in 2019. Product revenue was $1,204 million in 2019, compared to $1,090 million in 2018.

cases.description: Baseline B1: Product revenue 2019 changed 1,204 -> 1,312; total left at 1,514. No numeric prose, so only arithmetic can fire.
cases.derivation: 2019: 1312+310=1622 vs 1514, discrepancy 108 > 1.5 -> contradiction. 2018 still adds up.

cases.description: Consistency-preserving edit: Product revenue 2019 -> 1,312 and Total revenue 2019 -> 1,622. No numeric prose. Expected MISS.
cases.derivation: 1312+310=1622 and 1090+295=1385, so every arithmetic check passes although the table is poisoned.

cases.description: Same consistent edit as case 03, but the surrounding prose was left unchanged.

detector_input.pre_text: ACME Corp revenue by type is shown below.
detector_input.post_text: Total revenue was $1.5 billion in 2019. Product revenue was $1,204 million in 2019, compared to $1,090 million in 2018.

cases.derivation: Arithmetic passes (case 03). $1.5B vs 1,622M: 122M > 50.5M tolerance. $1,204M vs 1,312M: 108M > 1M. 2018 product claim matches.

cases.description: Consistent table edit AND prose rewritten to match. Internally consistent but wrong. Expected MISS.

detector_input.pre_text: ACME Corp revenue by type is shown below.
detector_input.post_text: Total revenue was $1.6 billion in 2019. Product revenue was $1,312 million in 2019, compared to $1,090 million in 2018.

cases.derivation: $1.6B vs 1,622M: 22M <= 50.5M. Product claims match exactly. Nothing on the page disagrees, so D1 cannot detect it.

cases.description: Components printed to one decimal sum to 99.9 while the total shows 100.0.
cases.derivation: Discrepancy 0.1. Tolerance = 4 printed values x 0.05 = 0.2. Passes.

cases.description: Same as 06 but total 100.2: more than rounding can explain.
Parentheses and '$ (150)' denote negatives; totals only add up if they are read as negative.
cases.derivation: 2019: 5400-1200-150=4050. 2018: 4900+350-75=5175. Reading parentheses as positive would give 6750 and 5325 (fail).

cases.description: A dash in a component cell. D1 must not treat it as zero by default.
cases.derivation: 2019: 120+80=200 checked and passes. 2018 has a dash -> skipped as missing_value (would pass only if the dash were assumed to be 0).

cases.description: Total assets = Total current assets + Property + Goodwill; Cash and Receivables must not be counted twice.
cases.derivation: 100+250=350. Contiguous hypothesis for Total assets: 400+150=550 (fails); nested hypothesis: 350+400+150=900 (passes). Double counting would give 1250.

cases.description: Cash changed 100 -> 130 with no totals updated.
cases.derivation: Total current assets: 130+250=380 vs 350 -> fail. Total assets uses the printed subtotal 350: 350+400+150=900 -> pass. Exactly one contradiction.

cases.description: Person 2-style unit attack: unit note changed 'in millions' -> 'in thousands'. Prose still says $1.5 billion.
cases.derivation: Arithmetic is scale-free and passes. 1,514 thousand = 1,514,000 vs 1,500,000,000 -> prose contradiction.

cases.description: Title says thousands, unit note says millions. Prose comparison cannot be aligned.
cases.derivation: Arithmetic passes (2 checks). The prose claim is skipped as table_scale_ambiguous, not passed.

cases.description: Prose mentions net revenue, a year not in the table, and a narrower scope; only the last sentence is comparable.

detector_input.post_text: Net revenue was $1.9 billion in 2019. Revenue was $1.5 billion in 2017. Revenue from services was $0.4 billion in 2019. Revenue was $2.0 billion in 2019.

cases.derivation: 'Net revenue' is a different metric (qualifier). 2017 is not a column. 'Revenue from services' is a narrower scope. Each of these would be a false contradiction if compared. 'Revenue ... $2.0 billion in 2019' matches 2,000M exactly.

cases.description: Simulated parsing error: a label and value merged, so the last row has too few cells.
cases.derivation: Column alignment cannot be trusted -> no checks; must be reported as NOT_CHECKABLE, not as passing.

cases.description: The parser found no table on the page.
A 'Less:' row is subtracted but printed positive; D1 does not guess the sign.
cases.derivation: Summing would give 700 vs 300 (false alarm). The relationship is unsupported -> uncheckable.

cases.description: A 'Total' column summing quarterly columns, including negative returns.
Person 2-style header attack: the 2019 and 2018 headers are swapped; values unchanged; prose unchanged.

detector_input.post_text: Total revenue was $1.5 billion in 2019. Product revenue was $1,204 million in 2019, compared to $1,090 million in 2018.

cases.derivation: Sums still hold per column. Now 2019 total = 1,385 (|1500-1385|=115 > 50.5), product 2019 = 1,090 (vs 1,204) and 2018 = 1,204 (vs 1,090): three prose contradictions.

cases.description: A change amount ('increased by $114 million') must not be compared with a level cell.

detector_input.post_text: Product revenue increased by $114 million to $1,204 million in 2019.

cases.derivation: '$114 million' is in a change clause -> skipped. '$1,204 million in 2019' is a level and matches.
